title: Banks closed on September 11? Union announces strike, warns of more in September and October- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: If you have urgent branch related work such as cash deposits, cheque clearance, loan processing or KYC updates try to complete it before September 11.   September 09, 2026 / 08:10 IST             Banking services could see disruption starting Friday as the United Forum of Banking Unions (UFBU) has called a one-day nationwide strike on September 11. This is just the start. UFBU has also announced a three-day strike on September 28. 29 and 30, and warned of an indefinite strike from October 26 if things stay unresolved. The core issues A long pending demand for a 5-day work week which was agreed upon in the 12th Bipartite Settlement back in March 2024, but never implemented. The union is also protesting the government’s new Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, calling it discriminatory, along with pension related grievances Talks between UFBU and the Indian Banks’ Association on September 4 failed to find a middle ground and break the deadlock. In a X post, UFBU said the meeting “did not yield any positive outcomes” and that the strike will go ahead as planned September 11 falls on a Friday, followed by the weekend, which means that costumers could face upto 3-4 days of disruption. Public sector banks are likely to see the biggest impact. What should you do? Net banking, UPI, Mobile banking and ATMs will remain unaffected unless notified to users for scheduled maintenance or otherwise. Follow us on:

If you have urgent branch related work such as cash deposits, cheque clearance, loan processing or KYC updates try to complete it before September 11.

September 09, 2026 / 08:10 IST

Banking services could see disruption starting Friday as the United Forum of Banking Unions (UFBU) has called a one-day nationwide strike on September 11.

This is just the start. UFBU has also announced a three-day strike on September 28. 29 and 30, and warned of an indefinite strike from October 26 if things stay unresolved.

The core issues

A long pending demand for a 5-day work week which was agreed upon in the 12th Bipartite Settlement back in March 2024, but never implemented.

The union is also protesting the government’s new Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, calling it discriminatory, along with pension related grievances

Talks between UFBU and the Indian Banks’ Association on September 4 failed to find a middle ground and break the deadlock.

In a X post, UFBU said the meeting “did not yield any positive outcomes” and that the strike will go ahead as planned

September 11 falls on a Friday, followed by the weekend, which means that costumers could face upto 3-4 days of disruption.

Public sector banks are likely to see the biggest impact.

What should you do?

Net banking, UPI, Mobile banking and ATMs will remain unaffected unless notified to users for scheduled maintenance or otherwise.

Additionally, customers relying on cheque clearance should also account for the possible delays.
